issues: Beige background, black doodle and a grey-white window: the three fidelity levels looked the same in colour, like a wireframe
The doodle appeared fully drawn and static, so the first level lacked the act of an idea being sketched
Message text was 27px, channels 19px and sidebar labels 13px, still unreadable after the push-in
Generic placeholder content (four messages, five channels): busy, no hero and no full stop at the end
changes: Look switched to porcelain: cobalt marker sketch → cool grey-blue skeleton → full-colour UI (navy sidebar, cobalt accent), so fidelity also climbs in colour
The sketch draws itself stroke by stroke over 16f on dotted paper, then boils every 4f; the swap is an 8f ease-in shrink-out with the skeleton springing in on the same frame
The UI is redesigned for camera: a fictional Parlor #launch channel with three messages, 30px names, 40px body and 32–40px channels in a centred 1480×820 window
Rhythm reworked: skeleton rows slide in → one shimmer pass → 1.08 push-in while the sidebar and header develop first and three rows develop word by word 14f apart
The last word 'today?' lands 14f late in bold cobalt with one overshoot, followed by ~30f of clean hold
